Header: Fusarium oxysporum f.sp. lentis Amharic: yeferafira zenbe; Tigrigna: fire hamema

Prevention: Plant resistant varieties such as alemaya or chalew
Rotate lentil crops with cereals (maize, wheat, sorghum) for 4-5 years.
This will reduce the disease inoculum in the soil
Avoid planing a new crop near land previously affected by the disease and make sure the soil is well drained
Before planting, infected crop debris should be destroyed by burning
Avoid injuring plant stems and roots when weeding
Minimise movement of soil and plant material between affected and uneffected areas and clean farm tools by heating with fire to sterilise
Ensure that seed production does not take place on affected farms as the disease may be seed borne
Monitoring: The disease can occur in both seedling and adult plants.
Monitor the crop from emergance to maturity
Seedlings: look for sudden drooping of the plant followed by drying of leaves and death.
The roots might be reduced but can appear healthy with no internal discolouration
Adult plants: symptoms usually appear from flowering to late pod-filling.
Look for sudden drooping of the upper leaves, dull green colour of leaves followed by wilting and drying/ yellowing of the whole plant or individual stems then death
Internal root/stem symptoms show dark discolouration of the vascular tissues
Take action when the very first sings of the disease are seen on a single plant
Direct Control: Pull out the affected plants, as well as healthy plants 5-10 metres into the area surrounding the patch and burn them in the patch
Control run off water from infected areas to clean areas to avoid spreading the pathogen
Start working from disease free areas before proceeding to affected parts of the field to avoid spreading the disease
Restrictions: There are no chemicals registered in
Ethiopia currently for management of this disease
